papers.title: Highly processed foods can be considered addictive substances based on established scientific criteria
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Applies established tobacco-addiction criteria to highly processed foods.
papers.one_line_claim: Highly processed foods can meet the same scientific criteria used to label tobacco as addictive: compulsive use, psychoactive effects, reinforcement, and craving.

papers.title: Is Food Addictive? A Review of the Science
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Narrative review synthesizing biological and behavioral parallels with substance addiction.
papers.one_line_claim: Ultra-processed foods high in added fat and refined carbohydrate show biological and behavioral parallels with addictive substances.

papers.title: Ultra-Processed Diets Cause Excess Calorie Intake and Weight Gain: An Inpatient Randomized Controlled Trial of Ad Libitum Food Intake
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Inpatient RCT: matched meals, yet UPF drove extra calorie intake and weight gain.
papers.one_line_claim: Even when meals are matched for calories and macros, an ultra-processed diet leads people to eat ~500 extra kcal/day and gain weight.

papers.title: Social, clinical, and policy implications of ultra-processed food addiction
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Policy analysis that assumes the addiction framing rather than a new trial.
papers.one_line_claim: Treating ultra-processed foods as addictive substances would change clinical care and food policy, not just personal willpower.

papers.title: “Eating addiction”, rather than “food addiction”, better captures addictive-like eating behavior
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Widely cited critique: substance-based food addiction evidence is poor; behavior is the better frame.
papers.one_line_claim: “Food addiction” is a misnomer: evidence for a substance-based addiction to specific foods is poor; addictive-like eating is better described as a behavioral eating addiction.

papers.title: Obesity and the brain: how convincing is the addiction model?
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Influential review arguing the addiction model of obesity is not well supported.
papers.one_line_claim: The brain-addiction model of obesity is not convincing: key features of drug addiction do not map cleanly onto overeating.

papers.title: The concept of “food addiction” helps inform the understanding of overeating and obesity: NO
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Point/counterpoint “NO” essay, not new experimental data.
papers.one_line_claim: The food-addiction concept does not usefully explain overeating and obesity compared with existing eating-disorder and behavioral frames.

papers.title: Halving warming with idealized solar geoengineering moderates key climate hazards
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Multi-model climate analysis of a half-warming solar-geoengineering scenario.
papers.one_line_claim: Offsetting about half of CO₂-driven warming with idealized solar geoengineering moderates key climate hazards in most regions rather than creating obvious regional losers.

papers.title: A temporary, moderate and responsive scenario for solar geoengineering
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Scenario paper arguing for limited, temporary, responsive deployment — not a full earth-system trial.
papers.one_line_claim: Solar geoengineering could be used temporarily, moderately, and responsively to slow warming while emissions fall — not as a permanent substitute for cutting carbon.

papers.title: 20 reasons why geoengineering may be a bad idea
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Commentary listing risks; influential but not a new empirical study.
papers.one_line_claim: Blocking sunlight to cool Earth may be a cure worse than the disease: ozone, weather disruption, termination shock, and a moral hazard against cutting emissions.

papers.title: Potentially dangerous consequences for biodiversity of solar geoengineering implementation and termination
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Models climate-velocity impacts on biodiversity from rapid start or sudden stop.
papers.one_line_claim: Sudden termination of solar geoengineering would more than double climate velocities, pushing biodiversity hotspots faster than species can track.

papers.title: Reflecting Sunlight
authors: Board on Atmospheric Sciences and Climate
Division on Earth and Life Studies
National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine
papers.evidence_strength_reason: National Academies assessment: research agenda, not a recommendation to deploy.
papers.one_line_claim: A National Academies assessment treats sunlight reflection as a research topic with large governance and risk gaps — not as a technology ready to deploy.

papers.title: Why nuclear energy is sustainable and has to be part of the energy mix
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Advocacy review arguing fission is the only developed source at the needed scale.
papers.one_line_claim: Nuclear fission is the only developed source that can deliver industrial-scale, reliable, low-carbon power; wind and solar need backup that is usually fossil.

papers.title: Key role for nuclear energy in global biodiversity conservation
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Multi-criteria ranking of electricity sources for biodiversity and cost.
papers.one_line_claim: Among major electricity sources, nuclear and wind rank highest on benefit-to-cost for biodiversity; shutting nuclear off the table risks more land-hungry generation.

papers.title: Evaluation of a proposal for reliable low-cost grid power with 100% wind, water, and solar
papers.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Peer critique documenting modeling errors in a 100% WWS-without-nuclear proposal.
papers.one_line_claim: A widely cited 100% wind-water-solar roadmap (no nuclear) relies on invalid modeling and unsupported assumptions; a diverse clean portfolio including dispatchable plants is more feasible.

papers.title: 100% clean and renewable wind, water, and sunlight (WWS) all-sector energy roadmaps for the 50 United States
papers.evidence_strength_reason: State-level WWS roadmaps arguing nuclear is unnecessary; later heavily critiqued.
papers.one_line_claim: Each U.S. state could convert all energy uses to wind, water, and sunlight by 2050 — nuclear is not required in these roadmaps.

papers.title: The Future of Nuclear Energy in a Carbon-Constrained World
papers.evidence_strength_reason: Major lab study: nuclear can help decarbonize, but cost has risen and expansion prospects are dim.
papers.one_line_claim: Nuclear can cut the cost of deep decarbonization in models, but new plants have only gotten more expensive — cost, not physics, is the barrier to replacing fossil fuels.
